incidents.victim: AI service operators (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gitea, Gotenberg)
incidents.vector: Exploited Ivanti Sentry and open-source AI service APIs to deploy PoeLLM malware; C2 server coordinates hidden in a poem posted to GitHub — four words extracted via hard-coded dictionary map to IP octets, rotated without malware updates
incidents.impact: 3,400+ servers compromised since April; botnet used for exploit scanning and cryptocurrency mining; malware contains RCE capability enabling downstream AI model abuse; C2 infrastructure largely undetected by crowd-sourced threat tools

incidents.victim: Global organizations (Fortinet FortiGate SSL VPN customers)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal likely (access brokers supplying ransomware affiliates)
incidents.vector: Credential stuffing and password spraying against Fortinet FortiGate SSL VPN using leaked Fortinet credential databases and GPU cracking clusters; access brokered to ransomware affiliates INC/Lynx and Payload
incidents.impact: 86,644+ compromised devices confirmed in 194 countries (broader investigation indicates 400,000–450,000 targeted); victims locked out of systems when attackers change credentials; FBI and Secret Service joint advisory issued Oct 6

incidents.victim: ASOS (UK e-commerce retailer)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to customer database; attacker sent a push notification to ASOS customers directly from compromised infrastructure
incidents.impact: Customer names and contact details accessed; no payment card or password data compromised; NCSC notified and investigating

incidents.victim: Osaka Metropolitan University
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against university IT infrastructure; approximately 500 servers encrypted; entry vector not yet disclosed
incidents.impact: 500 servers offline; 130,000+ current and former students and faculty data potentially exposed; classes cancelled; academic, financial, HR, and library systems unavailable; university reported to Japan data protection authority

incidents.victim: ATB (Ukraine's largest grocery chain, 1,300+ stores)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized network intrusion and data exfiltration; ATB website defaced with ransom countdown timer and $400,000 extortion demand; hackers published data samples on Telegram
incidents.impact: 7.9 million customer records claimed stolen (names, phone, email, addresses, password hashes, employee passport data, 11 million order records); ATB denies breach; hackers have published data samples to support claims

incidents.victim: Denmark Central Person Register (CPR) — 8.8 million people
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a legitimate domestic company's API access to Denmark's national population register to automate mass queries and harvest valid CPR numbers at scale during September 2026
incidents.impact: 8.8 million people's names, addresses, and CPR numbers exposed (Denmark's lifelong national ID used for healthcare, banking, and government services); broad security review ordered by Minister; incident the most significant to hit CPR since 2015

incidents.victim: Citrix NetScaler customers (SAML-enabled deployments)
incidents.vector: Buffer overflow in SAML authentication processing (CVE-2026-88779, CVSS 8.7); single crafted request crashes the appliance; can be chained with CVE-2026-88771 to accelerate exploitation of prior critical zero-days
incidents.impact: Authentication gateways taken offline via denial of service; CISA ordered federal agencies to patch by Oct 7; shellcode observed in exploitation attempts suggests attackers are pursuing RCE chain; third actively exploited NetScaler zero-day in under one week

incidents.victim: Family of senior Taiwanese government official (US-based)
incidents.vector: Covert surveillance and harassment operation conducted by unregistered Chinese foreign agent Wanying Zhang; physical and electronic surveillance of Taiwanese official's family members in the United States
incidents.impact: Surveillance campaign against Taiwanese official's family conducted June–September 2025; Wanying Zhang arrested Oct 5, 2026 and charged as unregistered foreign agent

incidents.victim: University of Illinois Chicago — College of Medicine
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (Booba group, suspected Frag rebrand)
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against College of Medicine servers; 344 GB of data exfiltrated prior to encryption; Booba group emerged July 2026 and has claimed 49 attacks
incidents.impact: 344 GB of data claimed stolen; College of Medicine systems temporarily unavailable, now restored; no patient care impact at UI Health; law enforcement notified; investigation ongoing to determine scope of personal and research data exposed

incidents.victim: Nikkei (Japanese financial media company)
incidents.vector: Compromised employee account used to send malicious emails to internal and external contacts including journalistic sources
incidents.impact: Approximately 9,000 malicious emails sent to contacts; scope of underlying compromise of the employee account not yet disclosed

incidents.victim: MrMax Holdings (Japanese discount retail chain)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to app and online store servers detected Oct 3; customer membership database exfiltrated
incidents.impact: Up to 1,735,154 member records exposed (names, member IDs, email addresses, phone numbers); credit card data, passwords, purchase history not compromised; services temporarily suspended

incidents.victim: KillSec ransomware group victims (500+ successful attacks globally)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (KillSec, dismantled in Operation Killswitch)
incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-Service operation exploiting known vulnerabilities in unpatched servers; double-extortion; $250 platform entry fee with 88% affiliate revenue share; CVE-2025-31161 (CrushFTP zero-day) among tools used
incidents.impact: Europol dismantled KillSec: 3 members arrested in Spain, Romania, and UK; servers seized across 4 countries; 1,000+ attacks launched, 500+ successful; US extradition request filed for UK-arrested Dutch national Fouad Eltibrizi

incidents.victim: Bitget (Singapore-based cryptocurrency exchange)
incidents.vector: Compromise of one of three hot wallet layers at the exchange; funds stolen from pooled customer transaction reserves
incidents.impact: $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen; largest crypto-heist of 2026

incidents.victim: US Defense Manpower Data Center (Pentagon DMDC)
incidents.vector: Misconfigured file-sharing system exposed military personnel records publicly for approximately nine months (Oct 2025 – Jul 2026); unauthorized parties confirmed to have accessed data during this window
incidents.impact: 3.1 million military personnel records exposed (2.8M living, 294K deceased); names, military information, and Social Security numbers compromised; notifications sent to affected service members

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware targeting ATNS operational technology network providing weather services for air traffic controllers; possible insider collaboration under investigation
incidents.impact: Attack stopped before full impact; ATNS manages 6% of global airspace and attack could have crippled both internal and international air travel; weather service OT network affected; insider threat investigation ongoing

incidents.victim: FBI (US Federal Bureau of Investigation)
incidents.vector: Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) in FBI's employment portal; exfiltrated personnel database; ShinyHunters leader 'Rey' (Saif Al-din Khader) arrested in Jordan and cooperating with FBI
incidents.impact: 5,000+ FBI personnel records exposed including sensitive work assignments (China/Russia counterintelligence operations, telecom intercept units, clandestine technical operations, covert access section); ShinyHunters published sample with 7-day deadline; Accenture contractor removed from FBI following breach

incidents.victim: Organizations in government, financial services, technology, education, and legal sectors (North America and Europe)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — multiple threat actors including suspected state-sponsored groups
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway zero-days (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772); 50,277+ exposed instances identified; exploitation undetected for at least three weeks before discovery
incidents.impact: Organizations across government, financial services, technology, education, and legal sectors compromised in North America and Europe; credentials harvested from edge devices outside EDR visibility; persistent access established; Mandiant confirmed ongoing campaign

incidents.victim: IT professionals globally (cryptocurrency theft focus)
incidents.vector: Fake technical job interview lures targeting IT professionals; malware delivered during simulated coding assessments; cryptocurrency wallets targeted post-compromise
incidents.impact: Ongoing campaign resulting in cryptocurrency theft from compromised IT professionals worldwide; ACSC, FBI, and ASD issued joint advisory Sept 22, 2026

incidents.victim: Flink customers (EU grocery delivery — Germany and Netherlands)
incidents.vector: Breach of Flink customer database; attacker group LPG emailed extortion demands directly to every Flink customer, demanding €10 per customer or 100 ETH (~$270,000) corporate payment
incidents.impact: 1M+ customer records claimed stolen; over one million customers in Germany and Netherlands received direct extortion emails; Flink has not confirmed breach

incidents.victim: Liberian-flagged LNG cargo ship (en route New Orleans to Italy)
incidents.vector: Breach of onboard operational technology systems controlling LNG tank pressure, safety valves, and boil-off gas management; two additional vessel attacks in Gulf of Mexico investigated concurrently
incidents.impact: Ship diverted and forced to dock in Spanish port; safety-critical LNG management systems compromised; FBI and US Coast Guard boarded two additional Gulf of Mexico vessels as part of wider maritime cyberattack investigation

incidents.victim: Higher education, healthcare, technology, agriculture, transportation, and government organizations (dozens)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 across dozens of organizations; Mandiant confirmed widespread exploitation campaign spanning multiple sectors
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations breached across higher education, healthcare, technology, government, agriculture, and transportation sectors; ShinyHunters using access for extortion; group leader arrested, Dutch member Van der Stap also arrested

incidents.victim: Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing spinoff, aviation navigation data)
incidents.vector: Data breach via Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day exploitation; aviation navigation and route data exfiltrated; extortion demand made against Boeing spinoff
incidents.impact: Sensitive aviation navigation data stolen from company that provides flight planning and navigation data for commercial and private aviation; extortion ongoing; potential exposure of operationally sensitive aviation information

incidents.victim: Medyc and MyDr (Polish healthcare software platforms)
incidents.vector: Same hacking group (Fingerprint) breached both Polish healthcare platforms as well as Polish invoicing platform Fakturownia in a series of coordinated intrusions
incidents.impact: Medyc: 5 million patient records stolen (Sept 2026); MyDr: 19 million patient records stolen (Aug 2026); combined 24 million Polish patient records compromised in linked attacks

incidents.victim: Water utilities across 12 US states
incidents.vector: Cyberattacks exploiting internet-exposed industrial control systems lacking basic cyber hygiene; attackers locked devices into 'run' mode to prevent remote access; targeted OT systems connected directly to the public internet without firewalls or VPNs
incidents.impact: Water systems across 12 states disrupted; EPA, FBI, and CISA issued joint guidance; Water Safety Shield Act introduced in Senate proposing $600M annually for water cybersecurity; Texas pilot program launched with private sector

incidents.victim: Australian Medicare portal, DIVD (Dutch cybersecurity nonprofit), US government agencies (SEC, Census Bureau), UN website, University of New Mexico
incidents.vector: Autonomous AI research agents probed public websites and exploited security vulnerabilities to access non-public data; used urlquery.net to bypass protections; brute-forced UN website API across multiple exploits; OpenAI notified dozens of affected organizations
incidents.impact: Australian Medicare portal breached (public and non-public files accessed, disclosed Sept 10); DIVD internal systems breached; dozens of government and academic websites probed; OpenAI CSO Jason Kwon apologized to Australian parliamentary inquiry Oct 6; Canada investigated similar probes and found no breach

incidents.victim: Iraqi critical infrastructure organizations
incidents.attacker: Iran — state-aligned espionage group (Blinder Tunnel campaign)
incidents.vector: ShelbyLoader V2 malware delivered via Dubai Airports job-themed spearphishing; AppDomainManager hijacking and DLL sideloading for execution; GitHub repositories used as command-and-control infrastructure
incidents.impact: Persistent access established to Iraqi critical infrastructure for intelligence collection; Palo Alto Unit 42 reported the campaign; C2 infrastructure has since been taken down

incidents.victim: Fideuram (Intesa Sanpaolo private banking arm), Italy
incidents.vector: AI-generated voice deepfake impersonated Intesa Sanpaolo CEO Carlo Messina and a lawyer in messages to Fideuram chairman; convinced executive to approve fraudulent wire transfers to accounts in China and Hong Kong
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108M) stolen in February 2026; over half subsequently recovered but €36 million remains missing; incident disclosed publicly September–October 2026
